queGane.title: Que Gane el Mejor
queGane.subtitle: Real-time software that runs a live school competition show on TV Perú, migrated from Unity to a modern web stack.
about: “Que Gane el Mejor” is a TV Perú competition show that pits two schools against each other per episode, with teams of seven high-school seniors competing in knowledge games.
It airs live, with games like “Personajes” and “Mi libro favorito”, and grand finals bringing together hundreds of students from schools across the country.

system.label: Real-time:
system.text: manages the on-screen games, scores and show flow live

system.label: Operated from the switcher:
system.text: I operate it myself during the broadcast

system.label: No downtime:
system.text: any failure must be recovered within seconds, live on air

system.label: Sole developer:
system.text: I build and maintain it on my own

role.title: Migration from Unity to the web
role.body: I migrated the entire system from a Unity application to a modern web stack: Next.js deployed on Vercel, Supabase for storage, database and access control, and Cloudflare. It is live on air today. I use Vercel's deploy-based versioning for instant rollback: if a version fails, I revert to the previous one without taking the show off the air.

role.title: Live editor and load-first architecture
role.body: I built an online editor to reposition images, video and backgrounds live — impossible with the previous Unity build. All on a load-first architecture, with careful RAM management to guarantee interruption-free rendering during the live show.

role.title: Data pipeline and daily operation
role.body: Production uploads the day's data to the cloud and the system downloads it to run the show. A “live” and “sample” data scheme lets hosts review the information from tablets and lets production fix data instantly from behind the cameras.

role.title: Live audience voting
role.body: I developed a QR-based voting system for viewers to back a school, with anti-abuse protections backed by Cloudflare Tunnel to prevent multiple votes and attacks.

impact.title: In production, on air
impact.desc: System running live on national television across multiple seasons, with zero on-air failures.

impact.title: Migrated to web without taking the show off air
impact.desc: The system moved from Unity to Next.js / Vercel / Supabase while the show was on air, using instant rollback as a safety net.

impact.title: National reach
impact.desc: Over 600 students from 28 schools across different regions of Peru.

impact.title: Sole developer
impact.desc: Design, development and live operation by a single person.

pukllaspa.title: Pukllaspa Yachay
pukllaspa.subtitle: The origin of the live system I operated for TV Perú: a daily quiz show in Quechua, built and operated in real time.
about: Pukllaspa Yachay (“Learning by Playing”) was a TV Perú competition show to promote learning the Quechua language, with a daily contest between three participants.
It aired live in prime time for about two and a half years. It was the first program I built the system for, and the starting point of everything that came after.

system.label: Real-time:
system.text: control of the show flow, rounds and scores live

system.label: Daily data:
system.text: each broadcast required new questions, images and per-game structures

system.label: Fault-tolerant:
system.text: rollback-based versioning to recover within seconds live on air

role.title: Real-time competition system
role.body: I developed in Unity/C# the software that controls the live show: participant management, rounds, and 20+ interactive on-screen games, each with its own scoring system, operated by me during the broadcast.

role.title: Daily data collector
role.body: Since the show aired daily, I built a separate system to load each broadcast's data — questions, images and different structures per game — so production could prepare the day's content without touching the game software.

role.title: Live reliability
role.body: I implemented a rollback-based versioning scheme: the system ran the latest version but could fall back to a previous one if something failed. On a live show any error had to be resolved within seconds, and the system ran full seasons with zero on-air failures.

role.title: Integration with production
role.body: The software integrated with TV Perú's production to control on-screen graphics, scores and transitions between show segments.

impact.title: Live national broadcast
impact.desc: Program aired in prime time on TV Perú for about two and a half years.

impact.title: Failure-free operation
impact.desc: The system ran full seasons live, recovering within seconds from any incident.

impact.title: Foundation for what followed
impact.desc: The system I built here was the starting point of the one that now runs “Que Gane el Mejor”, already migrated to web.

impact.title: Cultural preservation
impact.desc: A contribution to promoting and teaching the Quechua language in Peru.
